verdicts.quote: "Both OAuth apps and GitHub Apps use OAuth 2.0." ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/creating-an-oauth-app))
verdicts.reason: Public OAuth 2.0 flows are supported; per rubric we prefer OAuth2 when available. JWT is used by GitHub Apps to obtain installation tokens, not as the primary multi-tenant user authorization method.

verdicts.quote: "You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to." ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/creating-an-oauth-app))
verdicts.reason: Credentials (OAuth apps/GitHub Apps) are self-serve; no partner gating to start.

verdicts.quote: "Manage repositories and code Manage issues, pull requests, and projects Automate CI/CD workflows … Manage organizations and teams" ([github.com](https://github.com/github/docs/blob/main/content/rest/index.md))
verdicts.reason: Official REST docs enumerate dozens of resource categories across the product, indicating broad coverage.
The MCP server is published under the github org and explicitly labeled official.

verdicts.quote: "You can register a GitHub App under your personal account or under any organization you own." ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/creating-github-apps/registering-a-github-app))
verdicts.reason: Self-serve app registration plus comprehensive REST docs mean Composio could ship now without needing partner access or app review.
